title: Smoked Garam Masala Tandoori Chicken
headnote: Tested with 2½ lb (1,134 g) boneless chicken thighs; the marinade tasted good. Reconstructed from a chef's video and scaled to a half batch. The tested batch used 2 Tbsp of 2–3-year-old Kashmiri chili powder (1 Tbsp initially, then 1 Tbsp more), which produced less vibrant red color than the video. Try fresh Kashmiri chili powder for stronger color; 1 Tbsp is the original half-batch quantity.

ingredientGroups.title: Marinade
items: 1–2 Tbsp Kashmiri chili powder (2 Tbsp used in successful test with older powder)
¼ cup kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), loosely packed
9 g (1 Tbsp) Diamond Crystal kosher salt

steps: Gently warm the oil, then remove from heat. Stir in Kashmiri chili powder and smoked garam masala; bloom for 20–30 seconds without scorching.
Allow the spiced oil to cool slightly, then stir in the garlic paste and ginger paste.
Crush the kasuri methi between your palms and mix into the spiced oil with the Diamond Crystal kosher salt.
Stir in the thick yogurt until the marinade is uniform and clings thickly to a spoon.
Coat the chicken thoroughly, cover, and refrigerate for 6–12 hours.
Grill or roast over high heat until lightly charred and the thickest pieces reach 165°F internally. Cooking method and time were not recorded for the successful test.
reviewFlags: Cooking equipment and actual cook time not recorded; finish method supplied as guidance. Exact chef ingredient volumes were estimated from video screenshots.
sourceNote: User-tested adaptation of a restaurant chef's tandoori marinade shown in video screenshots. Original cookbook Tandoori Chicken recipe remains unchanged. This version uses ¼ cup oil and 1 Tbsp each garlic and ginger paste as a subsequent adjustment.
